content: Sodium dichloroisocyanurate is a chemically stable compound that serves as a source of chlorine. It is widely utilized as a disinfectant, biocide, industrial deodorant, and detergent. In small quantities, it is commonly found in water purification tablets or filters. Chemically, sodium dichloroisocyanurate is the sodium salt of dichloroisocyanuric acid. Products containing this compound may also include cyanuric acid. It is white in color and typically appears in the form of crystallized granules, powder, or tablets. Structurally, it is a heterocyclic ring compound derived from triazine. The compound is reactive with water, urea, ammonia, reducing agents, and strong bases. When it reacts, it can release toxic fumes, including chlorine gas. From a safety perspective, environments where sodium dichloroisocyanurate is handled should be equipped with proper ventilation systems or appropriate respiratory protection devices. Individuals handling this chemical should wear protective gloves and clothing to minimize exposure. Symptoms of exposure include coughing, a sore throat, redness of the skin or eyes, chemical burns, pain, and in severe cases, loss of vision. Prolonged or repeated exposure can lead to dermatitis. If ingested, the affected individual should rest, rinse their mouth with water, and seek medical attention. Vomiting should not be induced. In the event of a fire, containers of the substance may be cooled with water spray, provided that the chemical does not come into direct contact with water. Spills of this compound should not be washed into public sewage systems.
